# Three.js

WebGL scene-graph library. Used at `^0.185.1` in [[stickfps]], and there only — it is the single
instance of 3D rendering in the source set.

## How it is used: primitives all the way down

There is **no asset pipeline**. No `.glb`, no textures on disk, no fonts. `Environment.tsx` builds
the entire arena out of box, plane and cylinder geometry in 576 lines; the stickmen are generated
procedurally; textures are inline-SVG data URIs. That constraint is deliberate and predates the code
— see [[no-external-assets]].

The practical consequence is that the whole visual identity lives in code that diffs, tests and
reviews like code, and that a design change is an edit rather than a re-export. The cost is that
everything costs geometry setup time, and that the art ceiling is set by what you can express in
primitives.

Three.js is consumed through [[react-three-fiber]] rather than directly — imperative `scene.add`
calls are rare in the client.

## Three gotchas the build actually hit

These are worth recording because all three cost a round each and none are obvious from the API:

- **A mesh parented to the camera is invisible unless the camera is itself a descendant of `scene`.**
  The first-person weapon rig in [[stickfps]] attached correctly, rendered nothing, and was
  `return null`ed for two rounds before the real cause was found.
- **The default directional-light shadow camera is a ±5 m box.** An arena larger than that renders
  near-black outside it, which reads as "lighting is broken" rather than "the shadow frustum is
  small".
- **Lighting intensities are unit-sensitive across versions.** Values tuned for legacy lighting units
  produce a scene far darker or brighter than intended after the physically-correct default.

Lighting broke twice in total: once too dark to read cover by, once near-black from the shadow
camera.

## Vendored knowledge about it

The repo commits 19 Three.js "skill packs" — 87 files of reference tables and NEVER/ALWAYS rules —
alongside the product. That is documented as its own habit in [[agent-skills-checked-into-the-repo]],
including the version mismatch between what the packs declare and what the project runs.
